l3s.name: Life & Annuity Application Intake & Suitability Review

l4s.name: Application receipt, good-order review and case setup

steps.name: Receive Life & Annuity Application Package
steps.description: Receive new life and annuity applications via e-app, producer portal or paper ACORD life application forms (application parts, agent's report, HIPAA and FCRA authorizations, signed illustration), log the new business case and index all documents.
steps.supporting: Policy Data Entry Clerk, Underwriting Assistant
steps.inputs: ACORD life/annuity application package, agent's report, HIPAA and FCRA authorizations, signed point-of-sale illustration
steps.outputs: Logged new business case, indexed application documents

steps.name: Verify Producer License & Appointment
steps.description: Confirm the writing producer holds an active state license, line-of-authority and carrier appointment for the product and state of sale before the case proceeds; hold cases written by unappointed or lapsed producers. The producer licensing and appointment program itself is owned by Distribution & Channel Management (PG-16-02) — this is the in-flow gate only.
steps.supporting: New Business Case Manager, Compliance Analyst
steps.inputs: Producer identification, state license and line-of-authority records, carrier appointment data
steps.outputs: Producer license and appointment verification, held cases for unappointed producers

steps.name: Perform Good-Order Review & Resolve NIGO Items
steps.description: Check the application against the good-order checklist (signatures, state-required forms, completed health and avocation questions, beneficiary designations, premium mode), flag not-in-good-order defects and chase the producer until the case is in good order.
steps.supporting: Policy Data Entry Clerk, Underwriting Assistant
steps.inputs: Indexed application documents, good-order checklist, state form requirements
steps.outputs: Good-order determination, NIGO defect list, producer follow-up requests

steps.name: Screen Applicant & Owner Against Sanctions Watchlists
steps.description: Screen the proposed insured, owner and payor against OFAC SDN and consolidated sanctions lists and complete customer identification checks before the contract can be issued; escalate true matches to the financial crime team and block the case.
steps.supporting: Financial Crime AML Officer, New Business Case Manager
steps.inputs: Applicant and owner identity data, OFAC SDN and consolidated screening lists, customer identification program rules
steps.outputs: Screening disposition, cleared case or blocked-party escalation

steps.name: Establish Underwriting Case & Order Database Checks
steps.description: Open the underwriting case in the workbench and order the instant database evidence common to every underwriting path — MIB inquiry, prescription (Rx) history and MVR checks — deferring paramedical exam and APS orders until the accelerated-vs-full underwriting path is assigned, so fluidless-eligible cases are not knocked out by unnecessary exams.
steps.inputs: Good-order application, age-and-amount requirements grid, evidence vendor ordering services
steps.outputs: Opened underwriting case, ordered database checks (MIB, Rx, MVR), pending path-dependent requirements list

steps.name: Communicate Case Status & Outstanding Requirements
steps.description: Keep the producer and applicant informed of case status, chase aging outstanding requirements on a defined cadence, and manage cycle-time expectations through evidence-gathering delays such as APS turnaround.
steps.inputs: Case status, outstanding requirements list, aging thresholds
steps.outputs: Producer and applicant status notifications, aging requirement follow-ups

steps.name: Identify Replacement Activity & Issue Required Notices
steps.description: Detect replacement or 1035 exchange activity from the application's replacement questions, obtain the signed Notice Regarding Replacement and comparison disclosures per NAIC Model #613, and notify the existing insurer in writing within five business days of application receipt as the model regulation requires.
steps.inputs: Replacement questions on application, existing coverage details, NAIC Model #613 notice forms
steps.outputs: Replacement identification, signed Notice Regarding Replacement, existing-insurer notification within five business days, policy comparison summary

steps.name: Review Replacement & Suitability
steps.description: Review annuity and life applications for replacement activity and best-interest/suitability compliance: validate replacement disclosure forms, assess the producer's recommendation against the consumer's profile per NAIC Model #275's care/disclosure/conflict/documentation obligations (NY Reg 187 for New York business), and document the insurer's review before issue.
steps.supporting: New Business Case Manager, Compliance Analyst
steps.inputs: Application, replacement disclosure and comparison forms, consumer suitability/best-interest profile, producer recommendation documentation, existing-policy details
steps.outputs: Suitability determination, replacement compliance confirmation, documented basis of recommendation, declined/escalated cases

steps.name: Conduct Supervisory Review & Disposition Escalations
steps.description: Apply the insurer's NAIC Model #275 supervision system to escalated cases: second-line review of unsuitable or conflicted recommendations, rejection or conservation of the transaction, and referral of producer conduct patterns for remediation or termination.
steps.supporting: Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager, Annuity Suitability Analyst
steps.inputs: Suitability determination, escalated cases, producer conduct history
steps.outputs: Supervisory sign-off, rejected or conserved unsuitable transactions, producer remediation referrals

steps.name: Triage Case & Determine Underwriting Path
steps.description: Apply accelerated-underwriting eligibility rules — using the application disclosures and the MIB, Rx and MVR database results ordered at case setup — to route each case down the fluidless/algorithmic path or full medical underwriting, and confirm which age-and-amount evidence requirements actually apply to the assigned path.
steps.supporting: Underwriting Assistant, New Business Case Manager
steps.inputs: Good-order case, MIB/Rx/MVR database results, accelerated underwriting eligibility rules, age-and-amount requirements grid
steps.outputs: Underwriting path assignment, confirmed evidence requirements, accelerated-path disqualification triggers

steps.name: Order & Evaluate Medical and Financial Evidence
steps.description: Order the path-specific evidence dictated by the age-and-amount requirements grid — paramedical exam, attending physician statements (APS) and financial questionnaires — and evaluate it alongside the MIB inquiry, prescription (Rx) and MVR results from case setup, identifying impairments, avocation/aviation risks and red flags for the risk classification decision.
steps.supporting: New Business Case Manager, Underwriting Assistant
steps.inputs: Life/annuity application, HIPAA and FCRA authorizations, MIB inquiry results, Rx and MVR reports, paramedical exam results, attending physician statements, financial questionnaires
steps.outputs: Evidence assessment, identified impairments and red flags, requirements follow-up list

steps.name: Resolve Discrepancies & Order Additional Requirements
steps.description: Reconcile conflicts between the application, MIB alerts and received evidence; order follow-up requirements (additional APS, labs, EKG, specialist questionnaires) and consult medical resources on complex impairments before classification.
steps.supporting: Medical / Nurse Case Manager, Underwriting Assistant
steps.inputs: Evidence assessment, MIB alerts, conflicting medical or avocation disclosures
steps.outputs: Additional evidence orders, reconciled discrepancies, updated underwriting case file

steps.name: Perform Financial Underwriting & Justify Face Amount
steps.description: Validate insurable interest and that the requested face amount is financially justified against income-multiple and net-worth guidelines, total in-force and applied-for coverage, and the stated purpose of insurance.
steps.inputs: Financial questionnaires, income and net-worth documentation, existing in-force and applied-for coverage totals
steps.outputs: Insurable-interest confirmation, justified face amount, financial underwriting notes

steps.name: Assign Risk Class & Table Rating
steps.description: Classify the risk against the underwriting manual into preferred/standard/substandard classes, applying table ratings (A-P / 1-16, typically +25% mortality per table), flat extras or exclusion riders for substandard impairments and avocations.
steps.inputs: Evidence assessment, underwriting manual, mortality and impairment guidelines
steps.outputs: Risk class assignment, table rating or flat extra, proposed exclusion riders

steps.name: Refer Excess-Retention Cases to Reinsurance
steps.description: For face amounts above the company retention schedule or jumbo-limit cases, obtain automatic treaty capacity confirmation or place facultative reinsurance, and incorporate reinsurer offer terms into the underwriting decision.
steps.supporting: Facultative Reinsurance Specialist / Underwriter, Ceded Reinsurance Analyst
steps.inputs: Risk class assignment, face amount, retention schedule, treaty terms
steps.outputs: Facultative cession placement, reinsurer offer terms, net retention confirmation

steps.name: Render Approve, Rate, or Decline Decision
steps.description: Within delegated authority limits (with referral above), render the final approve-as-applied, rated counteroffer, postpone or decline decision, documenting the rationale and any reinsurance dependencies in the case file.
steps.inputs: Evidence assessment, risk class and rating, reinsurance confirmation, authority limits
steps.outputs: Underwriting decision (approve/rate/decline/postpone), counteroffer terms, decision rationale documentation

steps.name: Issue Adverse Action Notices & Report MIB Codes
steps.description: For declined, postponed or rated decisions based wholly or partly on consumer reports, issue the FCRA Section 615(a) adverse action notice naming the report sources and the applicant's dispute and free-report rights; separately submit coded findings of underwriting significance to MIB per member reporting rules — codes reflect the findings, not the decision, and are reported whether or not the case outcome is adverse.
steps.inputs: Underwriting decision, consumer report sources used, findings of underwriting significance, MIB coding guidelines
steps.outputs: FCRA adverse action notice, MIB code submission, applicant information-rights disclosure

steps.name: Communicate Offer & Manage Counteroffer Acceptance
steps.description: Communicate the underwriting offer to the producer, quote the amended premium for rated counteroffers, and capture the applicant's signed acceptance amendments or withdrawal before the case moves to issue.
steps.inputs: Underwriting decision, counteroffer terms, amended premium quote
steps.outputs: Offer communication to producer, accepted or withdrawn counteroffers, signed amendment forms

l3s.name: Life Policy Issue, Delivery & In-Force Placement

l4s.name: Policy issuance, delivery requirements and free look

steps.name: Prepare Policy for Issue & Calculate Premium
steps.description: Build the issue-ready policy record from the approved decision — final risk class, ratings, riders, premium mode and billing elections — calculate the modal premium and set up the billing account for handoff to Billing, Collections & Receivables.
steps.supporting: Policy Data Entry Clerk, Billing Operations Manager
steps.inputs: Approved underwriting decision, final risk class and rating, premium mode and billing elections
steps.outputs: Issue-ready policy record, calculated modal premium, billing account setup

steps.name: Generate Policy Contract & Disclosure Package
steps.description: Assemble the policy contract from state-approved forms with schedule pages, riders and amendments, attach required disclosures (conformed illustration, buyer's guide, policy summary, free-look notice) and prepare delivery instructions including e-delivery consent.
steps.inputs: Issue-ready policy record, state-approved forms library, conformed illustration, buyer's guide and policy summary
steps.outputs: Assembled policy contract, required disclosure package, delivery instructions

steps.name: Deliver Policy & Collect Delivery Requirements
steps.description: Deliver the policy physically or electronically and collect outstanding delivery requirements — signed amendments, statement of good health, delivery receipt — together with the initial premium, tracking the delivery window so the contract does not lapse unplaced.
steps.supporting: Policy Issue Specialist, Broker Support Specialist
steps.inputs: Assembled policy contract, delivery requirements list, e-delivery consent, initial premium remittance
steps.outputs: Delivered policy, signed delivery requirements, collected initial premium

steps.name: Place Policy In Force & Trigger Commission Payment
steps.description: Verify all delivery requirements and the initial premium are received, set the policy to in-force status with the correct effective date, apply the premium, and release the commission feed to distribution compensation (commission calculation and payment are owned by Distribution & Channel Management, PG-16-03).
steps.inputs: Signed delivery requirements, initial premium, commission schedule
steps.outputs: In-force policy status, applied premium, commission feed to distribution compensation

steps.name: Administer Free-Look Cancellations & Refunds
steps.description: Process free-look returns within the state-mandated window (typically 10-30 days, 30 days for replacement policies per NAIC Model #613): void the policy, refund the full premium, reverse policy values and notify distribution of commission chargebacks.
steps.supporting: Policy Issue Specialist, Payment Processing Clerk
steps.inputs: Free-look cancellation request, state free-look period rules, premium received
steps.outputs: Voided policy, full premium refund, commission chargeback notification

steps.name: Hand Off Case to Policy Administration & Close
steps.description: Transfer the in-force policy and complete case file to ongoing policy administration and servicing (in-force transactions live in CI-04-05), flag any outstanding post-issue service items, archive case documentation and close the new business case.
steps.supporting: Policy Issue Specialist, Policy Admin Ops Lead
steps.inputs: In-force policy record, complete case file, outstanding post-issue service items
steps.outputs: Closed new business case, policy administration handoff, archived case documentation

notes: Relocated step CI-06-05-S02 'Review Replacement & Suitability' absorbed verbatim (lightly adapted description adds NY Reg 187 mention) as step 2 of L4 'Replacement and best-interest suitability review' under L3 'Life & Annuity Application Intake & Suitability Review'; it carries that L4's deliverable (Suitability & Best-Interest Determination, SOR Underwriting Workbench).

Relocated step CI-06-05-S01 'Order & Evaluate Medical and Financial Evidence' absorbed as step 2 of L4 'Underwriting evidence acquisition and evaluation'; its original outputs bundled evidence assessment + risk class + approve/rate/decline — those decision outputs were split out into the dedicated 'Assign Risk Class & Table Rating' and 'Render Approve, Rate, or Decline Decision' steps in the 'Risk classification and underwriting decision' L4 so the L5 sequence stays granular and ordered.

Shared-stream references honored, not duplicated: enterprise sanctions/AML program = RC-20-05; escheatment/unclaimed property = F-11-05 (and life DMF matching = CI-04-05-S05); complaints = OC-14; in-force life/annuity transactions (surrenders, loans, 1035 disbursement) = CI-04-05; commission calculation/payment = Distribution & Channel Management PG-16-03 (this stream only triggers the commission feed and chargebacks); ongoing billing/invoicing = CI-01 (this stream only sets up the billing account at issue).

One in-flow sanctions step retained ('Screen Applicant & Owner Against Sanctions Watchlists') because OFAC requires blocking before contract issuance and the same in-flow pattern already exists in CI-06-01 ('Perform Clearance & Sanctions Screening') and CI-04-05-S03; the program-level screening/SAR machinery stays in RC-20-05.

Producer license/appointment verification is an in-flow gate only; the producer licensing/appointment program itself lives in Distribution & Channel Management PG-16-02 (Producer Licensing Coordinator leads the check).
No P&C L3 names reused: existing Submission-to-Bind L3s (Submission Intake, Risk Assessment, Terms & Governance, Bind & Handover) avoided; all three L3s are life/annuity-specific.

All leads/supporting are verbatim role-inventory names, weighted to the Life & Retirement set (New Business Case Manager, Life Underwriter, Annuity Suitability Analyst, Policy Issue Specialist, Life Policy Service Representative, Billing Operations Manager) with day-to-day doers as leads; sorApplication values (Underwriting Workbench, Policy Administration Platform) are verbatim from app-inventory.json.

Regulatory anchors validated by research: NAIC Model #275 best-interest (care/disclosure/conflict/documentation + insurer supervision system) and NY Reg 187; NAIC Model #613 replacement notices; FCRA adverse action + MIB coding; ACORD life application form series and ~60% industry NIGO rates justify the dedicated good-order step; state free-look 10-30 days (30 for replacements). Sources: https://content.naic.org/cipr-topics/annuity-suitability-best-interest-standard, https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/model-law-275.pdf, https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/model-law-613.pdf, https://hexure.com/what-are-not-in-good-order-nigo-rates//, https://acord.org/standards-architecture/acord-data-standards/Life_Annuity_Data_Standards, https://www.insurance.com/life-insurance/life-insurance-basics/table-ratings.html, https://www.westernsouthern.com/life-insurance/what-is-a-life-insurance-free-look-period, https://www.insurtechexpress.com/life-insurance-edelivery-the-future-of-policy-delivery-is-already-here/

REVIEW FIX (flow order): the original design ordered paramedical exams and APS at case setup, then ran accelerated-underwriting triage afterwards — backwards for an AU-era flow, where fluidless eligibility is decided before any exam is ordered. Case-setup step renamed 'Establish Underwriting Case & Order Database Checks' and now orders only the instant database evidence (MIB, Rx, MVR); paramed/APS ordering moved into the post-triage 'Order & Evaluate Medical and Financial Evidence' step, and the triage step now consumes the database results.

REVIEW FIX (MIB accuracy): MIB code reporting was wrongly tied only to adverse decisions; per MIB member rules, coded findings of underwriting significance are reported regardless of case outcome, while the FCRA Section 615(a) adverse action notice is the adverse-decision-specific obligation. Step description corrected. Sources: https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/consumer-reports-what-insurers-need-know, https://www.mib.com/mib_faq.html

REVIEW FIX (Model #613 precision): replacing insurer must notify the existing insurer in writing within five business days of application receipt — 'within required timeframes' tightened to the explicit five-business-day deadline, and the 30-day replacement free look attributed to Model #613. Source: https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/model-law-613.pdf

REVIEW FIX (life-only rule): all three L3 names were generic enough to read as P&C areas; renamed to 'Life & Annuity Application Intake & Suitability Review', 'Life Underwriting & Mortality Risk Classification', and 'Life Policy Issue, Delivery & In-Force Placement'. Verified no collision with any existing L3/L4 name in vs-outline.json.

REVIEW VERIFICATION: programmatic check confirmed every lead/supporting role (21 distinct) is verbatim in role-inventory.json and both sorApplication values are verbatim in app-inventory.json; the only step-name matches against vs-outline.json are the two CI-06-05 steps this stream is mandated to absorb (they still appear under Submission-to-Bind in the outline pending their removal there). Annuity suitability precedes issue (intake L3 before issue L3) and free-look administration is kept here as a new-business-window event distinct from CI-04 in-force servicing.

REVIEW NOTE (no change): suitability-before-issue, delivery-requirements/placement, conditional initial-premium handling, FCRA adverse action and reinsurance excess-retention referral were checked against industry practice and found correctly ordered; no contestability/1099-R obligations apply to this stream (those belong to life claims and retirement distribution streams).

steps.name: Receive & Authenticate Change Request
steps.description: Accept beneficiary, ownership/assignment, name and address change requests across channels, authenticate the policy owner and confirm signing authority (POA, trustee, guardianship), and open a service case in the policy administration system.
steps.supporting: Customer Service Rep, Annuity Service Specialist
steps.inputs: Change request forms, policy record, owner identity verification, authority documentation
steps.outputs: Authenticated change request, opened service case

steps.name: Validate Consent & Designation Requirements
steps.description: Verify consent requirements before processing: irrevocable beneficiary written consent, spousal consent in community-property states, assignee acknowledgment for collateral assignments, and minor-beneficiary trust/UTMA arrangements; reject not-in-good-order requests with deficiency letters.
steps.inputs: Authenticated change request, current beneficiary designation, irrevocable beneficiary flags, state consent rules
steps.outputs: Validated designation change, consent evidence on file, deficiency letters

steps.name: Update Policy Record & Endorse Contract
steps.description: Apply the validated change to the policy master record, generate the endorsement or designation confirmation reflecting the new beneficiary/owner/assignee of record, and version the contract file for audit traceability.
steps.supporting: Life Policy Service Representative, Policy Admin Ops Lead
steps.inputs: Validated designation change, policy master record, endorsement templates
steps.outputs: Updated policy record, endorsement document, audit trail entry

steps.name: Confirm Change & Notify Parties
steps.description: Issue written confirmation of the recorded change to the owner and affected parties (prior irrevocable beneficiaries, assignees), post documents to the self-service portal, and close the service case with quality sampling.
steps.supporting: Policy Issuance / Document Fulfillment Specialist, Quality Assurance Analyst (Service)
steps.inputs: Updated policy record, endorsement document, party contact preferences
steps.outputs: Confirmation letters, portal-posted documents, closed service case

l4s.name: Inforce Financial Transactions, Disbursements & DMF Compliance

steps.name: Receive & Validate In-Force Transaction Request
steps.description: Accept life/annuity in-force financial transaction requests (surrender, partial withdrawal, policy loan, annuitization election, ownership-linked disbursements), verify owner identity and signing authority, confirm forms are in good order, and log the transaction in the policy administration system.
steps.supporting: Annuity Service Specialist, Retirement Operations Administrator
steps.inputs: Transaction request forms (surrender, withdrawal, loan, annuitization), policy record, identity and authority verification
steps.outputs: Good-order transaction request, verified owner authority, logged transaction case

steps.name: Review Replacement & Suitability Compliance
steps.description: For surrenders, exchanges (incl. 1035) and replacements, verify replacement notices and disclosures per NAIC Model #613, apply the best-interest/suitability review required by NAIC Model #275 (and NY Reg 187 where applicable) for annuity transactions, document the care/disclosure/conflict/documentation obligations, and route conservation or escalation where the transaction appears unsuitable.
steps.supporting: Compliance Analyst, Life Policy Service Representative
steps.inputs: Good-order transaction request, replacement disclosure forms, suitability/best-interest documentation, existing contract surrender-charge data
steps.outputs: Replacement notices, suitability/best-interest determination, conservation or escalation cases

steps.name: Screen Payee Against Sanctions Watchlists
steps.description: Screen the payee, policy owner and any added/changed beneficiaries against OFAC SDN and consolidated sanctions lists before funds release; on a true match, block the transaction and policy interest, report to OFAC within 10 business days, and route blocked funds per OFAC requirements.
steps.inputs: Payee and owner identity data, beneficiary details, OFAC SDN and consolidated screening lists
steps.outputs: Screening result, cleared payee or blocked-transaction escalation and OFAC report

steps.name: Disburse Funds & Apply Tax Withholding
steps.description: Calculate surrender/withdrawal/loan values including surrender charges and market value adjustments, apply federal/state tax withholding elections, release funds to the cleared payee, update policy values and status in the system of record, and generate the 1099-R tax reporting record.
steps.inputs: Cleared transaction, surrender/loan value calculation, withholding elections, payee banking details
steps.outputs: Disbursed funds, updated policy values and status, 1099-R tax reporting record

steps.name: Perform Death Master File Matching & Escheatment Handoff
steps.description: Compare in-force and lapsed life policies, annuity contracts and retained asset accounts against SSA Death Master File updates at least semi-annually using fuzzy-match rules per state unclaimed life insurance benefits acts; initiate beneficiary location and outreach on matches; track dormant proceeds and hand qualified items to Finance for unclaimed-property due diligence and state remittance.
steps.supporting: Compliance Analyst, Life Policy Service Representative
steps.inputs: In-force and lapsed policy/contract records, SSA Death Master File updates, state unclaimed-property dormancy schedules
steps.outputs: DMF match list, beneficiary outreach cases, dormant-proceeds handoff to Finance escheatment process

steps.name: Receive Conversion or Exchange Election
steps.description: Capture the owner's term-conversion or IRC Section 1035 exchange election, confirm the request is signed and in good order, and open a conversion/exchange case linked to both the existing and target contracts.
steps.supporting: New Business Case Manager, Annuity Service Specialist
steps.inputs: Conversion/exchange election form, existing policy record, target product selection
steps.outputs: Logged conversion or exchange case, good-order confirmation

steps.name: Verify Conversion Eligibility & Credits
steps.description: Confirm the contract is within its conversion period, the target permanent product is on the eligible-conversion list, and the insured's original risk class carries over without new evidence of insurability; calculate any conversion credits or term-premium offsets.
steps.inputs: Conversion case, contract conversion provisions, eligible product list, original risk class
steps.outputs: Eligibility determination, conversion credit calculation, attained-age premium quote

steps.name: Coordinate 1035 Funds Transfer & Carrier Exchange
steps.description: For external and internal 1035 exchanges, execute absolute assignment paperwork, request and reconcile surrender proceeds from the ceding carrier, preserve cost-basis carryover for tax-free treatment, and track transfer aging against service standards.
steps.supporting: Life Policy Service Representative, Tax Analyst
steps.inputs: Exchange authorization, assignment forms, ceding carrier surrender values, cost-basis records
steps.outputs: Received exchange proceeds, carried-over cost basis, transfer status tracking

steps.name: Issue Converted or Exchanged Contract
steps.description: Issue the new permanent policy or annuity contract with carried-over risk class and basis, apply conversion credits to first premium, and deliver contract documents with required disclosures.
steps.supporting: New Business Case Manager, Policy Issuance / Document Fulfillment Specialist
steps.inputs: Approved conversion/exchange, conversion credits, contract data, disclosure requirements
steps.outputs: Issued converted contract, delivered policy documents, applied credits

steps.name: Terminate Prior Coverage & Reconcile
steps.description: Terminate or reduce the original term coverage or surrendered contract effective the conversion date, refund unearned premium, reconcile values between old and new contracts, and confirm completion to the owner and servicing agent.
steps.supporting: Policy Admin Ops Lead, Billing Coordinator
steps.inputs: Issued new contract, original contract record, unearned premium calculation
steps.outputs: Terminated prior coverage, premium refund, reconciliation confirmation to owner and agent

l4s.name: Life Premium Billing Handoff & Premium Application

steps.name: Establish Billing Mode & Schedule at Issue
steps.description: Set up the premium billing arrangement at policy issue or mode change — frequency, method (direct bill, EFT, list bill, payroll deduction), modal factors and planned-premium amounts for flexible-premium contracts — in the policy administration system.
steps.supporting: Billing Coordinator, Life Policy Service Representative
steps.inputs: Issued policy record, owner payment elections, modal premium factors, list-bill agreements
steps.outputs: Configured billing schedule, payment method enrollment

steps.name: Transmit Premium Due Feed to Billing
steps.description: Generate and transmit the recurring premium-due feed (anniversaries, modal due dates, planned premiums) to the enterprise billing platform that handles invoicing, cash collection and dunning, and reconcile feed acceptance counts.
steps.inputs: Configured billing schedules, policy status changes, premium rate tables
steps.outputs: Premium due feed, feed reconciliation report, billing exceptions list

steps.name: Apply Premiums to Policy Values
steps.description: Post collected premiums back to the policy: apply premium loads, allocate to funds or fixed account per owner instructions, deduct cost-of-insurance and expense charges for universal life, and update cash values and paid-to dates.
steps.supporting: Life Policy Service Representative, Annuity Service Specialist
steps.inputs: Collected premium postings, allocation instructions, COI and expense charge tables
steps.outputs: Applied premiums, updated cash values and paid-to dates, allocation confirmations

steps.name: Resolve Policy-Side Premium Application Exceptions
steps.description: Research collected premiums that cannot auto-apply to the policy (short pays versus planned premium, overpayments above contract limits, post-lapse receipts, MEC-limit breaches), resolve or refund within aging standards, route unidentified-remitter cash back to the enterprise billing cash-suspense process, and escalate systemic feed defects to the billing operations owner.
steps.supporting: Cash Application Specialist, Billing Operations Manager
steps.inputs: Policy-side application exceptions, aging reports, policy status data
steps.outputs: Cleared application exceptions, refunds issued, unidentified-cash handoff to Billing suspense process, exception root-cause log

steps.name: Trigger Automatic Premium Loans
steps.description: Where the automatic premium loan provision is elected and cash value is sufficient, advance the overdue premium as a policy loan at the end of grace, record loan principal and interest accrual, and notify the owner of the APL transaction.
steps.supporting: Billing Analyst, Policy Admin Ops Lead
steps.inputs: Overdue premium list, APL elections, available loan values
steps.outputs: APL loan transactions, loan balance updates, owner notifications

steps.name: Identify Premium Default & Start Grace Period
steps.description: Detect unpaid premiums at due date, suppress lapse processing for policies with a pending or approved waiver-of-premium disability claim (claim adjudication stays with the claims stream), start the contractual grace period (31 days/one month standard; for flexible-premium universal life, grace ends not less than 61 days after the lapse-notice mailing per NAIC Model #585), and flag contracts approaching grace expiry.
steps.supporting: Life Policy Service Representative, Policy Admin Ops Lead
steps.inputs: Premium due and payment records, grace period rules by product and state, waiver-of-premium claim flags, policy status
steps.outputs: Grace-period flagged policies, waiver-suppressed lapse exclusions, grace expiry watchlist

steps.name: Issue Grace & Lapse-Pending Notices
steps.description: Generate state-compliant grace, late-payment and pending-lapse notices to owners and any designated third-party/secondary addressees (senior-protection designee statutes), log proof of mailing, and route responses to conservation outreach.
steps.supporting: Policy Issuance / Document Fulfillment Specialist, Compliance Analyst
steps.inputs: Grace-period flagged policies, state notice requirements, third-party designee records
steps.outputs: Mailed grace and lapse-pending notices, proof-of-mailing log, conservation contact list

steps.name: Apply Nonforfeiture Option at Lapse
steps.description: At grace expiry without payment, apply the owner-elected or contract-default nonforfeiture option per the Standard Nonforfeiture Law (NAIC #808) — cash surrender, reduced paid-up, or extended term insurance — calculating values from the policy's nonforfeiture basis, honoring the owner's right to elect an alternative within 60 days of the due date.
steps.supporting: Actuarial Analyst, Policy Admin Ops Lead
steps.inputs: Lapsed policy list, nonforfeiture value tables, owner elections, outstanding loan balances
steps.outputs: Applied nonforfeiture option, recalculated coverage or surrender value, owner election confirmations

steps.name: Update Policy Status & Notify Owner
steps.description: Set the final policy status (lapsed, reduced paid-up, extended term, surrendered), release any cash surrender disbursement through the financial-transaction flow, and send the post-lapse status notice with reinstatement rights disclosure.
steps.supporting: Life Policy Service Representative, Policy Issuance / Document Fulfillment Specialist
steps.inputs: Applied nonforfeiture outcome, policy master record, reinstatement provisions
steps.outputs: Final policy status, post-lapse notices, reinstatement rights disclosure

steps.name: Report Lapse & Conservation Metrics
steps.description: Produce lapse-rate, grace-cure and conservation-save reporting by product and distribution channel for persistency management, and feed chronic-lapse signals to product and experience-study teams.
steps.inputs: Lapse and cure activity, conservation outcomes, persistency targets
steps.outputs: Lapse and conservation dashboard, persistency exception report

steps.name: Receive Reinstatement Application
steps.description: Accept the reinstatement application within the contractual window (minimum three years from lapse per NAIC #808), verify the policy was not surrendered for cash and the nonforfeiture period has not expired, and open the reinstatement case.
steps.supporting: New Business Case Manager, Customer Service Rep
steps.inputs: Reinstatement application, lapsed policy record, reinstatement eligibility rules
steps.outputs: Eligible reinstatement case, ineligibility decline letters

steps.name: Underwrite Evidence of Insurability
steps.description: Order and evaluate the health statement and, where age/amount/duration rules require, additional evidence (Rx check, APS) to render the satisfactory-evidence-of-insurability decision required for reinstatement.
steps.supporting: New Business Case Manager, Underwriting Assistant
steps.inputs: Reinstatement health statement, Rx and APS evidence, original risk class
steps.outputs: Insurability decision (approve/decline), documented underwriting rationale

steps.name: Calculate Back Premiums & Loan Interest Due
steps.description: Compute all overdue premiums with interest (capped at the statutory rate, typically 6%), plus reinstatement or repayment of any policy loans outstanding at lapse with accrued loan interest, and quote the total amount due to the owner.
steps.inputs: Lapse date, premium history, statutory interest rates, outstanding loan balances
steps.outputs: Reinstatement amount-due quote, payment instructions to owner

steps.name: Collect Funds & Restore Coverage
steps.description: Apply the collected reinstatement payment, restore the policy to premium-paying status with original values and riders, rebuild paid-to dates and loan balances, and issue the reinstatement confirmation.
steps.supporting: Cash Application Specialist, Policy Issue Specialist
steps.inputs: Approved reinstatement, collected funds, policy master record
steps.outputs: Reinstated policy record, restored values and riders, reinstatement confirmation

steps.name: Reset Contestability Tracking
steps.description: Restart the contestability period for statements made in the reinstatement application (as permitted by state law and contract), tag the policy for claims-stage review of reinstatement-era misrepresentation, and close the case with compliance sampling.
steps.inputs: Reinstated policy record, reinstatement application statements, state contestability rules
steps.outputs: Contestability tracking flag, closed reinstatement case, compliance sample log

l3s.name: Life Policy Values, Statements & Retirement Recordkeeping

steps.name: Run Valuation & Interest Crediting Cycles
steps.description: Execute the recurring policy-value cycles: credit declared and guaranteed interest, process index-segment crediting for IUL/FIA, apply COI and expense deductions, accrue loan interest, and validate cycle output against actuarial control totals.
steps.inputs: Declared crediting rates, index segment data, COI and expense tables, loan balances
steps.outputs: Updated cash and account values, crediting audit trail, cycle control report

steps.name: Produce In-Force Illustrations & Projections
steps.description: Fulfill owner and agent requests for in-force illustrations and projections compliant with the NAIC Life Insurance Illustrations Model (#582) — guaranteed and current-assumption scenarios, loan and premium-change what-ifs — using the illustration formats and actuary-certified assumptions developed and maintained by the product organization.
steps.inputs: Illustration requests, current policy values, certified illustration assumptions
steps.outputs: In-force illustrations, projection reports, request fulfillment log

steps.name: Generate Annual Policy & Contract Statements
steps.description: Compose the annual statement for each life policy and annuity contract — premiums paid, current cash/account value, loan activity, surrender value, death benefit, crediting detail and UL sustainability warnings — and quality-check against the policy system of record.
steps.supporting: Life Policy Service Representative, Policy Admin Ops Lead
steps.inputs: Cycle-end policy values, transaction history, statement templates, disclosure requirements
steps.outputs: Annual policy and contract statements, statement quality-check log

steps.name: Distribute Statements & Post to Portal
steps.description: Deliver statements via elected channel (mail, e-delivery), post to the customer self-service portal, track delivery failures and returned mail for address remediation, and confirm e-delivery consent records.
steps.supporting: Digital Channel Manager, Life Policy Service Representative
steps.inputs: Statement packages, delivery preferences, e-delivery consents
steps.outputs: Delivered statements, portal postings, returned-mail remediation queue

steps.name: Resolve Value Inquiries & Statement Disputes
steps.description: Research owner and agent questions about credited values, charges and statement figures, correct confirmed value errors with retroactive adjustments, and route formal complaints to the enterprise complaints process.
steps.inputs: Value inquiries, statement dispute cases, crediting audit trail
steps.outputs: Resolved inquiries, corrective value adjustments, complaint referrals

steps.name: Process Contributions & Allocation Instructions
steps.description: Receive plan-sponsor payroll contribution files and participant allocation/transfer instructions for group annuity and retirement contracts, post contributions to participant accounts at current unit values, and resolve file rejects with the sponsor.
steps.supporting: Retirement Operations Administrator, Cash Application Specialist
steps.inputs: Payroll contribution files, participant allocation instructions, unit values, plan provisions
steps.outputs: Posted participant contributions, executed transfers, reject resolution log

steps.name: Maintain Participant Records & Vesting
steps.description: Maintain participant demographic, deferral, beneficiary and vesting records per plan document rules, process enrollments and terminations, and apply vesting schedules to employer-source balances.
steps.inputs: Enrollment and termination feeds, plan vesting schedules, participant elections
steps.outputs: Current participant records, applied vesting balances, eligibility status updates

steps.name: Process Distributions, Rollovers & RMDs
steps.description: Execute participant distributions — terminations, hardships, in-service withdrawals, direct rollovers and IRC 401(a)(9) required minimum distributions — applying plan rules, spousal consent where required, 20% mandatory withholding on eligible rollover distributions, and 1099-R reporting.
steps.inputs: Distribution requests, RMD calculations, plan distribution rules, withholding elections
steps.outputs: Disbursed distributions and rollovers, RMD compliance log, 1099-R records
steps.deliverable: Participant distribution and RMD compliance record

steps.name: Prepare ERISA & DOL Disclosure Support
steps.description: Produce participant fee disclosures (ERISA 404(a)(5)), sponsor 408(b)(2) service-provider disclosures, benefit statements, and the recordkeeping data package supporting the sponsor's Form 5500 filing, tracking statutory delivery deadlines.
steps.inputs: Plan fee and expense data, participant balances, DOL disclosure requirements, filing calendars
steps.outputs: Fee disclosure packages, participant benefit statements, Form 5500 data package

steps.name: Reconcile Plan Assets & Resolve Breaks
steps.description: Reconcile participant-level recordkeeping balances to contract-level plan assets each cycle, investigate and correct breaks (late trades, mispostings, unit-value errors) including participant make-whole corrections, and certify the reconciliation to plan governance.
steps.supporting: Retirement Operations Administrator, AR Reconciliation Analyst
steps.inputs: Participant balance extracts, contract asset values, trade and posting logs
steps.outputs: Plan asset reconciliation, corrected breaks and make-whole adjustments, reconciliation certification

notes: Relocated steps absorbed: all five CI-04-05 steps (Receive & Validate In-Force Transaction Request, Review Replacement & Suitability Compliance, Screen Payee Against Sanctions Watchlists, Disburse Funds & Apply Tax Withholding, Perform Death Master File Matching) form their own L4 'Inforce Financial Transactions, Disbursements & DMF Compliance' under L3 'Life & Annuity Inforce Transactions & Disbursements', per the relocation mandate. The other life-relocations.json entries (CI-02-01-S07 death-claim validation, CI-06-05 new-business underwriting/suitability) belong to the life claims and life new-business streams, not this one, and were not absorbed here.

DMF step lightly adapted: state remittance and owner due diligence are NOT duplicated — the step ends in a 'dormant-proceeds handoff to Finance escheatment process', referencing the existing Finance F-11-05 L4 (Escheatment and unclaimed property reporting) which owns due diligence and state remittance. This L4 keeps only the insurer-specific DMF fuzzy matching and beneficiary outreach required by state Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits acts.

In-flow sanctions screening justified: 'Screen Payee Against Sanctions Watchlists' is retained inside the disbursement flow because OFAC requires pre-release screening and 10-business-day blocked-property reporting at the transaction point; the enterprise sanctions/AML program (list management, alert investigation, SAR/OFAC filings) remains in Risk & Compliance RC-20-05 and is referenced, not duplicated. Non-financial beneficiary/owner additions are screened via the same in-flow step (its scope covers 'added/changed beneficiaries'), so the non-financial changes L4 carries no separate screening step.

Shared-stream references (checked against vs-outline.json): invoicing, cash collection, dunning and receivables reconciliation stay in Billing CI-01 — this stream only owns the life-specific billing handoff (premium-due feed, premium application to policy values, APL); formal complaints route to Customer Service OC-14-03; general service inquiry intake/routing stays in OC-14-01/02; statement-dispute complaints are explicitly 'complaint referrals' to that stream.

No P&C L3 names reused: L3s are 'Life & Annuity Inforce Transactions & Disbursements', 'Life Premium Billing, Lapse & Reinstatement', and 'Life Policy Values, Statements & Retirement Recordkeeping' — none collide with CI-04's P&C areas (Policy Lifecycle, Policy Change Processing, Service Fulfillment, Complaint Resolution) or any other stream's L3 names.

Regulatory grounding: state standard-policy-provision laws (31-day/one-month grace), NAIC Standard Nonforfeiture Law #808 (60-day election window, cash surrender/RPU/ETI options, 3-year minimum reinstatement window, 6% max interest on back premiums, evidence of insurability), UL Model #585 (flexible-premium UL grace ends not less than 61 days after lapse-notice mailing), Replacement Model #613 and Suitability #275/NY Reg 187 (in the relocated suitability step), Illustrations Model #582 (in-force illustrations), IRC 1035 (exchanges, basis carryover), IRC 401(a)(9) (RMDs), ERISA 404(a)(5)/408(b)(2) and Form 5500 (retirement recordkeeping), state senior third-party-designee lapse-notice statutes, state Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits acts (semi-annual DMF matching), OFAC 31 CFR 501.603 (10-business-day blocked-property reports). Sources: NAIC model-law-808.pdf, model-law-585.pdf and model-law-613.pdf at content.naic.org.

Role discipline: leads are day-to-day doers from role-inventory.json verbatim, weighted to the Life & Retirement set (Life Policy Service Representative leads 10 steps; Retirement Recordkeeping Specialist, Retirement Operations Administrator, Policy Issue Specialist, Annuity Suitability Analyst, New Business Case Manager, Life Underwriter all lead steps). Billing Operations Manager appears as supporting (managerial), not lead. Disability roles are intentionally absent — disability case management/claims belong to a claims-side stream, not policy administration.

Deliverables: one per L4 on its pivotal step — Recorded beneficiary/ownership endorsement, Disbursement confirmation with 1099-R tax record, Issued converted/exchanged policy contract (all Policy Administration Platform); Reconciled life premium billing feed (Billing & Receivables System); Nonforfeiture option determination record, Reinstated policy confirmation, Participant distribution and RMD compliance record (Policy Administration Platform); Annual policy value statement package (Document & Forms Management). All sorApplication values verbatim from app-inventory.json; the inventory has no dedicated retirement recordkeeping system, so Policy Administration Platform is used as the closest SoR.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW FIX (accuracy): the grace-period step and regulatory note previously attributed the 61-day rule to 'universal life secondary guarantees per NAIC Model #585'. Verified against content.naic.org/model-law-585.pdf: the 61-day provision is the flexible-premium UL grace period, which ends not less than 61 days after the mailing of the required lapse-notice/report — it is not a secondary-guarantee provision. Step description and note corrected; the 31-day standard grace is now attributed to state standard-policy-provision laws, not SNFL #808 (which governs nonforfeiture values, the 60-day election, and reinstatement — those citations re-verified as correct).

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW FIX (duplication): 'Resolve Premium Suspense & Exceptions' overlapped Billing CI-01-02 steps 'Research Suspense Items'/'Resolve & Clear Suspense', which own unidentified-remitter cash suspense. Step renamed 'Resolve Policy-Side Premium Application Exceptions' and narrowed to exceptions that only exist at the policy level (short pays vs planned premium, overpayments/MEC limits, post-lapse receipts); unidentified cash is now an explicit handoff back to the CI-01-02 cash-suspense process.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW FIX (duplication): in-force illustration fulfillment kept here, but the illustration-development/certification work is owned by Product PG-18-02 ('Develop & Certify Product Illustrations' step found in vs-outline.json); the step description now references using the product organization's actuary-certified assumptions rather than implying this stream certifies them.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW FIX (missing industry step): lapse identification now suppresses lapse for policies with a pending or approved waiver-of-premium disability claim — standard carrier practice and a market-conduct exposure if omitted. Only the suppression check lives here; waiver-claim adjudication remains with the claims stream (Disability Case Manager deliberately not wired into this stream).

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW FIX (life-only L3 names): all three L3s renamed to carry the line of business explicitly — 'Inforce Policy Transactions & Disbursements' → 'Life & Annuity Inforce Transactions & Disbursements'; 'Premium Billing, Lapse & Reinstatement' → 'Life Premium Billing, Lapse & Reinstatement'; 'Policy Values, Statements & Retirement Recordkeeping' → 'Life Policy Values, Statements & Retirement Recordkeeping'. No remaining generic/P&C-sounding L3 names.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW VERIFICATION (no changes needed): every lead and supporting role across all 29 steps checked verbatim against role-inventory.json — all 30 distinct names match exactly, including the near-twin pair 'Cash Application / Billing Specialist' vs 'Cash Application Specialist' (both are real inventory entries and both are used intentionally). All sorApplication values ('Policy Administration Platform', 'Billing & Receivables System', 'Document & Forms Management') verified in app-inventory.json. Step ordering verified against practice: suitability/replacement review precedes sanctions screening which precedes disbursement; annuity suitability is handled pre-issue in CI-06-05 (new business) and pre-transaction here; retirement distributions carry 20% mandatory rollover withholding and 1099-R; reinstatement resets contestability only for reinstatement-application statements. Relocated CI-04-05-S01 was lightly split as permitted: its non-financial scope (beneficiary/ownership changes) is served by the dedicated 'Beneficiary, Ownership & Non-Financial Changes' L4, while the relocated step retains the financial-transaction scope.

steps.name: Receive Death Notification & Open Claim
steps.description: Capture the death notification from beneficiaries, agents, funeral homes or DMF referrals through any channel, record decedent and notifier details, open the claim case, and acknowledge receipt within the timeframes of the NAIC Unfair Claims Settlement Practices model.
steps.supporting: Contact Center Agent, Life Claims Examiner
steps.inputs: Death notification, decedent identifying details, notifier contact information, policy or contract number if known
steps.outputs: Opened claim case, notification acknowledgment, intake record

steps.name: Identify In-Force Policies & Contracts Across Lines
steps.description: Search policy administration, annuity and retirement recordkeeping systems for all life policies, annuity contracts, riders and retained asset accounts held by the decedent so every entitlement is claimed in one coordinated case, per NAIC Model #565 single-notice expectations.
steps.supporting: Annuity Service Specialist, Retirement Recordkeeping Specialist
steps.inputs: Decedent identifying details, policy administration records, annuity contract records, retirement account records
steps.outputs: Consolidated policy and contract inventory, linked claim sub-cases, coverage status confirmation

steps.name: Validate Death Certificate & Verify Beneficiary
steps.description: Obtain and validate the certified death certificate, verify beneficiary designation and claimant identity, flag policies within the two-year contestability period for underwriting review, and start the statutory death-benefit interest accrual clock. (Re-homed from Claims Intake-to-Settlement CI-02-01-S07.)
steps.supporting: Life Policy Service Representative, Compliance Analyst, Annuity Service Specialist
steps.inputs: Certified death certificate, claimant statement and ID, beneficiary designation on file, policy issue date
steps.outputs: Verified beneficiary entitlement, contestability flag, proof-of-loss receipt date, interest accrual start

steps.name: Assign Claim & Issue Acknowledgment Packet
steps.description: Route the verified claim to a life claims examiner based on product, complexity and contestability flags, and send the beneficiary an acknowledgment packet describing required documents, settlement options and expected timeframes.
steps.supporting: Claims Director / Manager, Life Claims Examiner
steps.inputs: Verified death claim file, examiner workload and authority levels, acknowledgment letter templates
steps.outputs: Assigned claim, beneficiary acknowledgment packet, claim service-level clock

l4s.name: Claim requirements gathering and good-order management

steps.name: Determine Claim Requirements by Product & Jurisdiction
steps.description: Build the requirements list for each beneficiary and contract: claimant statements, tax certifications, foreign-death documentation, assignments and collateral interests, community-property spousal considerations, and guardianship or estate papers for minor or estate beneficiaries.
steps.supporting: Life Policy Service Representative, Compliance Analyst
steps.inputs: Verified death claim file, product and rider provisions, state documentation requirements, beneficiary designations
steps.outputs: Claim requirements list per beneficiary, jurisdiction-specific forms list, special-handling flags

steps.name: Issue Claimant Statements & Claim Kits
steps.description: Send each beneficiary the claimant statement, settlement option election form and tax withholding forms through their preferred channel, without charging fees for the claim process as prohibited by NAIC Model #565.
steps.inputs: Claim requirements list, claimant contact details, claim kit templates, settlement option forms
steps.outputs: Issued claim kits, delivery confirmations, pending requirements register

steps.name: Track Outstanding Requirements & Follow Up Within Regulatory Timeframes
steps.description: Monitor outstanding requirements, issue periodic follow-ups and status letters within state unfair-claims-settlement-practices timeframes, and escalate aged claims so proceeds are not left pending without documented diligent effort.
steps.inputs: Pending requirements register, regulatory response timeframes, claim aging reports
steps.outputs: Follow-up correspondence, status letters, aged-claim escalations, compliance timestamps

steps.name: Review Submissions for Good Order & Authenticate Claimants
steps.description: Review returned documents for completeness and authenticity, authenticate claimant identity against KYC standards, resolve not-in-good-order items, and certify the claim file ready for adjudication.
steps.supporting: Compliance Analyst, Life Policy Service Representative
steps.inputs: Returned claimant statements and documents, identity verification results, good-order checklist
steps.outputs: Good-order certification, authenticated claimant record, adjudication-ready claim file

steps.name: Screen Claims for Contestability & Investigation Triggers
steps.description: Identify claims requiring special review: deaths within the two-year contestability period or after reinstatement, suicide-clause windows, foreign or undocumented deaths, missing-person presumptions, and fraud indicators warranting SIU referral.
steps.inputs: Good-order claim file, policy issue and reinstatement dates, cause and place of death, fraud indicator rules
steps.outputs: Contestable claim queue, SIU referrals, special-review routing decisions

steps.name: Conduct Contestable Claim Investigation
steps.description: For contestable claims, order attending physician statements, MIB and prescription histories, re-review the application against the evidence for material misrepresentation, and document findings for the rescission-or-pay decision.
steps.supporting: Life Underwriter, Medical Claims Reviewer, SIU Investigator
steps.inputs: Original application and underwriting file, attending physician statements, MIB and prescription histories, investigation authorizations
steps.outputs: Misrepresentation analysis, medical evidence summary, investigation findings file

steps.name: Determine Rescission, Adjustment or Payment Decision
steps.description: Render the adjudication decision with legal concurrence: pay in full, adjust the benefit, or rescind for material misrepresentation with premium refund, documenting the basis to withstand bad-faith and market-conduct scrutiny.
steps.inputs: Investigation findings file, policy provisions, state rescission standards, legal review notes
steps.outputs: Adjudication decision, rescission notice and premium refund where applicable, decision rationale documentation

steps.name: Identify Competing Claimant & Beneficiary Disputes
steps.description: Detect conflicting beneficiary designations, ex-spouse revocation statutes, slayer-statute allegations, estate and trust conflicts, and assignment disputes; attempt documented resolution with the parties before litigation.
steps.inputs: Beneficiary designations and change history, divorce decrees and court orders, claimant correspondence, state revocation and slayer statutes
steps.outputs: Dispute assessment, resolution attempts record, litigation referral where unresolved

steps.name: File Interpleader & Deposit Proceeds With Court
steps.description: Where entitlement cannot be safely determined, file an interpleader action, deposit the death benefit plus accrued interest with the court, and discharge the company from further liability among the competing claimants.
steps.inputs: Dispute assessment, death benefit and interest calculation, court filing requirements
steps.outputs: Interpleader filing, deposited proceeds, discharge of liability order

steps.name: Resolve Dispute & Release Proceeds Per Court Order
steps.description: Monitor the interpleader or settlement among claimants, implement the court order or signed release, distribute proceeds to the adjudicated beneficiaries, and close the dispute record.
steps.inputs: Court order or settlement agreement, deposited or held proceeds, adjudicated beneficiary entitlements
steps.outputs: Released proceeds, closed dispute record, updated claim file

l4s.name: Death benefit and statutory interest calculation

steps.name: Retrieve Policy Values & Adjustments
steps.description: Pull the date-of-death values for each contract: face amount, paid-up additions and dividends, rider benefits, outstanding policy loans and accrued loan interest, premium due or refundable, and recorded assignments or liens.
steps.supporting: Life Policy Service Representative, Annuity Service Specialist
steps.inputs: Policy and contract records, date of death, loan and dividend balances, assignment and lien records
steps.outputs: Date-of-death value extract, adjustment items list, rider benefit confirmation

steps.name: Calculate Gross Death Benefit & Deductions
steps.description: Compute the gross death benefit per contract provisions, apply deductions for loans, liens and premium due, add dividend and paid-up addition values, and produce the net benefit per beneficiary share.
steps.supporting: Actuarial Analyst, Life Policy Service Representative
steps.inputs: Date-of-death value extract, contract benefit provisions, beneficiary share percentages
steps.outputs: Gross and net benefit calculation, per-beneficiary allocation, calculation audit trail

steps.name: Calculate Statutory Claim Interest by State
steps.description: Apply each state's claim-interest statute from the required accrual date (date of death or proof of loss) at the prescribed rate through the payment date, and flag interest as taxable to the beneficiary for downstream 1099-INT reporting.
steps.inputs: Net benefit calculation, interest accrual start date, state interest rates and accrual rules
steps.outputs: Statutory interest amount, taxable interest flag, combined payable amount

steps.name: Obtain Settlement Authority Approval
steps.description: Route the calculated settlement through the claims authority matrix for peer review and management approval at the appropriate threshold, with quality review sampling before release to disbursement.
steps.supporting: Life Claims Examiner, Claims Quality Assurance / Training Manager
steps.inputs: Combined payable amount, authority matrix, adjudication decision, quality review checklist
steps.outputs: Approved settlement authority, quality review record, release-to-payment authorization

l4s.name: Accelerated death benefit and waiver-of-premium rider claims

steps.name: Receive Accelerated Benefit or Waiver-of-Premium Claim
steps.description: Capture accelerated death benefit claims (terminal or chronic illness) and waiver-of-premium disability rider claims on in-force life policies, confirm the rider is attached and premiums are current through the date of disability, open the living-benefit claim case, and issue physician certification forms.
steps.supporting: Life Policy Service Representative, Contact Center Agent
steps.inputs: Rider claim request, policy and rider record, premium payment status, physician statement forms
steps.outputs: Opened living-benefit claim case, rider attachment confirmation, issued certification forms

steps.name: Evaluate Medical Certification of Qualifying Condition
steps.description: Review the physician's certification against rider definitions — life expectancy of 12-24 months or less for terminal illness, inability to perform activities of daily living for chronic illness, or total disability satisfying the elimination period for waiver of premium — and order independent medical review where evidence is inconclusive.
steps.supporting: Disability Case Manager, Life Claims Examiner
steps.inputs: Physician certification, medical records, rider benefit definitions, elimination period requirements
steps.outputs: Qualifying-condition determination, independent review referrals, medical evidence file

steps.name: Approve Benefit & Calculate Acceleration or Waiver
steps.description: Approve or deny under claims authority; for accelerated benefits compute the payable amount with the actuarial discount or lien and the resulting reduction to the remaining face amount; for waiver claims set the waiver effective date back through the elimination period and suspend premium billing.
steps.inputs: Qualifying-condition determination, rider benefit formulas, face amount and policy values, premium schedule
steps.outputs: Benefit approval decision, acceleration calculation and face-amount reduction, waiver effective date

steps.name: Disburse Accelerated Benefit & Confirm Tax Treatment
steps.description: Pay the accelerated benefit to the sanctions-cleared owner or insured payee, update policy values and the remaining death benefit, and document the IRC 101(g) tax-exclusion status of terminal and chronic illness payments, with tax reporting where chronic-illness amounts exceed per-diem exclusion limits.
steps.supporting: Life Policy Service Representative, Tax Analyst
steps.inputs: Benefit approval decision, cleared payee instructions, IRC 101(g) exclusion limits, policy record
steps.outputs: Disbursed accelerated benefit, updated policy values and remaining death benefit, tax treatment documentation

steps.name: Recertify Continuing Disability & Terminate Waiver on Recovery
steps.description: Conduct periodic continuing-disability reviews on active waiver-of-premium claims, obtain updated physician certifications, and on recovery or rider termination resume premium billing and close the living-benefit claim.
steps.supporting: Medical Claims Reviewer, Billing Operations Manager
steps.inputs: Active waiver claim inventory, recertification schedule, updated physician certifications
steps.outputs: Continuing-eligibility determinations, resumed premium billing on recovery, closed waiver claims

steps.name: Present Settlement Options & Disclosures to Beneficiaries
steps.description: Provide each beneficiary the available settlement options — lump sum, interest option, fixed-period or fixed-amount installments, life income annuitization, and retained asset account — with the state-required disclosures, including that an RAA is not FDIC-insured and a lump sum is always available.
steps.supporting: Life Policy Service Representative, Annuity Service Specialist
steps.inputs: Approved settlement authority, settlement option provisions, RAA and annuitization disclosure forms
steps.outputs: Settlement options presentation, disclosure delivery record, election form issuance

steps.name: Record Settlement Election & Verify Payee Instructions
steps.description: Capture the beneficiary's settlement election and tax withholding choices, verify banking or payee instructions against the authenticated claimant record, and set up the payout structure for the elected option.
steps.supporting: Life Claims Examiner, Annuity Service Specialist
steps.inputs: Settlement election form, withholding elections, payee banking details, authenticated claimant record
steps.outputs: Recorded settlement election, verified payee instructions, configured payout structure

steps.name: Screen Beneficiary Payees Against Sanctions Lists
steps.description: Screen all payees against OFAC SDN and consolidated sanctions lists immediately before funds release, blocking and reporting true matches per OFAC rules. Required in-flow by regulation; the enterprise sanctions/AML program itself is governed in Risk & Compliance RC-20-05.
steps.inputs: Verified payee instructions, payee identity data, OFAC SDN and consolidated screening lists
steps.outputs: Screening result, cleared payee or blocked-payment escalation and OFAC report

steps.name: Disburse Proceeds & Apply Tax Withholding
steps.description: Release the death benefit plus statutory interest to cleared payees per the elected option, apply federal and state withholding, fund installment or annuitization structures, and post the disbursement to the claim and policy records.
steps.inputs: Release-to-payment authorization, cleared payees, combined payable amount, withholding elections
steps.outputs: Disbursed proceeds, funded settlement structures, posted payment records

steps.name: Issue Settlement Confirmation & Tax Reporting
steps.description: Send beneficiaries the settlement confirmation and explanation of benefits, and generate the tax reporting records — 1099-INT for claim interest and 1099-R where taxable distributions apply.
steps.inputs: Posted payment records, taxable interest flag, settlement election details
steps.outputs: Settlement confirmation letters, explanation of benefits, 1099-INT and 1099-R records

steps.name: Close Claim & Update Policy Status
steps.description: Terminate the policy or contract record, release any remaining reserves, complete the claim closure checklist, and feed claim outcome data to quality assurance and market-conduct reporting.
steps.supporting: Life Policy Service Representative, Claims Quality Assurance / Training Manager
steps.inputs: Disbursement confirmations, claim closure checklist, policy record
steps.outputs: Closed claim, terminated policy status, claim outcome data for QA and conduct reporting

steps.name: Establish & Fund Retained Asset Account
steps.description: Open the interest-bearing retained asset account for beneficiaries electing the RAA option, fund it with the full proceeds and accrued interest, and set the crediting rate per the account terms.
steps.inputs: RAA settlement election, disbursed proceeds amount, account terms and crediting rate
steps.outputs: Opened and funded RAA, account record, initial crediting rate setup

steps.name: Deliver RAA Disclosures & Welcome Kit
steps.description: Send the beneficiary the draft book or access instructions with the state-required RAA disclosures — full withdrawal always available, interest crediting basis, no FDIC insurance, guaranty association coverage limits — per the NAIC retained asset account guidance.
steps.inputs: Opened RAA, RAA disclosure templates, state disclosure requirements
steps.outputs: Delivered welcome kit, disclosure acknowledgment record, account access credentials

steps.name: Service RAA Drafts, Withdrawals & Statements
steps.description: Process drafts and withdrawal requests, credit interest, answer account-holder inquiries, and issue periodic statements and annual 1099-INT reporting on credited interest for active retained asset accounts.
steps.supporting: Payment Processing Clerk, Contact Center Agent
steps.inputs: Draft and withdrawal requests, account balances, interest crediting schedule
steps.outputs: Processed withdrawals, periodic account statements, interest tax reporting records

steps.name: Monitor RAA Dormancy & Refer to Escheatment
steps.description: Track account activity against state dormancy triggers, perform documented owner outreach on inactive accounts, and refer unresponsive dormant balances to the enterprise unclaimed-property process (Finance F-11-05) for due diligence and state remittance.
steps.inputs: Account activity history, state dormancy schedules, owner contact records
steps.outputs: Dormancy watch list, outreach attempt records, escheatment referrals to Finance

steps.name: Identify Maturing & Endowing Policies
steps.description: Run scheduled extracts to identify endowment policies reaching their endowment date and whole life policies reaching contractual maturity (age 100/121), and open proactive payout cases ahead of the maturity date.
steps.inputs: Policy administration extracts, maturity and endowment dates, insured attained-age data
steps.outputs: Maturity pipeline list, opened payout cases, advance notification schedule

steps.name: Notify Policyowners & Solicit Payout Elections
steps.description: Send advance maturity notices explaining the payout amount, available elections (lump sum, settlement options, extension where offered) and the tax character of any gain, and track responses through documented follow-up.
steps.inputs: Maturity pipeline list, owner contact records, maturity notice templates
steps.outputs: Maturity notices, payout election forms, response tracking record

steps.name: Calculate Maturity or Endowment Value
steps.description: Compute the maturity proceeds — guaranteed maturity value plus dividends and paid-up additions, less outstanding loans — and determine the taxable gain over cost basis for withholding and 1099-R reporting.
steps.inputs: Policy values at maturity, dividend and loan balances, cost basis records
steps.outputs: Maturity value calculation, taxable gain determination, withholding requirements

steps.name: Disburse Maturity Proceeds or Apply Election
steps.description: Pay the elected lump sum or fund the elected settlement option with applicable withholding, terminate the policy record, and issue the settlement statement and tax reporting to the policyowner.
steps.supporting: Life Policy Service Representative, Tax Analyst
steps.inputs: Maturity value calculation, payout election, payee instructions, withholding elections
steps.outputs: Disbursed maturity proceeds, terminated policy record, tax reporting records

steps.name: Refer Unresponsive Maturities to Unclaimed Property
steps.description: For owners who cannot be located or do not respond by the dormancy trigger, document the diligent search and refer the matured proceeds to the enterprise escheatment process (Finance F-11-05) for state remittance.
steps.inputs: Unresponsive maturity cases, owner search results, state dormancy schedules
steps.outputs: Documented diligent-search record, escheatment referrals, suspended payout cases

steps.name: Receive Annuity Death Claim & Confirm Contract Status
steps.description: Open the annuity death claim from the shared death-claim intake, confirm contract status and phase (accumulation versus payout), stop or adjust annuity payments as of the date of death, and recover any post-death overpayments.
steps.supporting: Life Claims Examiner, Retirement Operations Administrator
steps.inputs: Verified death claim file, annuity contract record, payment history, date of death
steps.outputs: Confirmed contract status, stopped or adjusted payments, overpayment recovery cases

steps.name: Determine Death Benefit Under Contract Provisions
steps.description: Value the death benefit per the contract — account value or return of premium at date of death, guaranteed minimum death benefit riders, payout-phase period-certain or refund balances — and document the valuation basis.
steps.inputs: Contract and rider provisions, date-of-death account values, GMDB rider terms, payout schedule balances
steps.outputs: Death benefit valuation, rider benefit determination, valuation basis documentation

steps.name: Capture Beneficiary Distribution Election
steps.description: Present and record each beneficiary's distribution election — lump sum, spousal continuation, five-year rule, life-expectancy stretch where permitted, or the SECURE Act ten-year rule for qualified contracts — with required disclosures for any annuitization election.
steps.supporting: Annuity Suitability Analyst, Retirement Recordkeeping Specialist
steps.inputs: Death benefit valuation, beneficiary type and relationship, qualified versus non-qualified status, distribution rule options
steps.outputs: Recorded distribution elections, spousal continuation setups, election disclosure records

steps.name: Process Qualified Contract & IRA Beneficiary Distributions
steps.description: For IRA and employer-plan annuities, apply IRS required-distribution and SECURE Act timing rules, ERISA spousal consent where applicable, establish inherited-account registrations, and coordinate plan-level reporting with recordkeeping.
steps.inputs: Recorded distribution elections, plan and IRA registration data, IRS distribution rules, spousal consent documentation
steps.outputs: Inherited account registrations, compliant distribution schedules, plan reporting records

steps.name: Disburse Annuity Death Proceeds & Issue Tax Reporting
steps.description: Release proceeds per the elected distribution after payee sanctions clearance via the shared settlement disbursement steps, apply withholding, and generate 1099-R reporting reflecting the taxable portion and distribution code.
steps.inputs: Compliant distribution schedules, cleared payees, withholding elections, taxable amount determination
steps.outputs: Disbursed death proceeds, updated contract status, 1099-R tax reporting records

steps.name: Receive DMF Match Referrals & Open Insurer-Initiated Claims
steps.description: Receive confirmed Death Master File matches from the servicing DMF comparison process (Policy Administration CI-04-05-S05), validate match quality, complete the documented good-faith effort to confirm the death within 90 days of the match as required by NAIC Model #565, and open insurer-initiated claims within the thorough-search timeframes of the company's multistate regulatory settlement agreement.
steps.supporting: Policy Admin Ops Lead, Compliance Analyst
steps.inputs: Confirmed DMF match list, match scoring rules, policy and contract records, RSA timeframe requirements
steps.outputs: Validated match queue, opened insurer-initiated claims, thorough-search clock start

steps.name: Conduct Beneficiary Location & Documented Outreach
steps.description: Perform the good-faith thorough search for beneficiaries using contact records, address and obituary searches and locator services, documenting at least the required outreach attempts and completing the search within the RSA's one-year window, at no charge to beneficiaries as required by NAIC Model #565.
steps.supporting: Life Policy Service Representative, Contact Center Agent
steps.inputs: Validated match queue, beneficiary contact records, locator service results, RSA outreach standards
steps.outputs: Documented search and outreach records, located beneficiary contacts, unlocatable determinations

steps.name: Adjudicate Located-Beneficiary Claims & Pay With Interest
steps.description: Move located beneficiaries into the standard requirements, adjudication and disbursement flow, paying the death benefit with statutory interest accrued from the date of death as required under DMF settlement practices.
steps.supporting: Payment Processing Clerk, Life Policy Service Representative
steps.inputs: Located beneficiary contacts, claim requirements packages, interest accrual from date of death
steps.outputs: Adjudicated insurer-initiated claims, paid benefits with accrued interest, closed match cases

steps.name: Track RSA Compliance & Report to Regulators
steps.description: Maintain the compliance record for the multistate regulatory settlement agreement and state unclaimed-benefits statutes — match volumes, search timeliness, payments and interest, and unlocatable proceeds referred to escheatment (Finance F-11-05) — and produce periodic reports for lead-state regulators and market-conduct exams.
steps.supporting: Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager, Life Claims Examiner
steps.inputs: Match and search activity records, payment and interest data, escheatment referral records, RSA reporting requirements
steps.outputs: RSA compliance metrics, regulator reports, market-conduct exam evidence, remediation actions
