steps.name: Receive & Register Disability Claim
steps.description: Accept STD/LTD claim notice from the employee, employer or portal; capture employee statement, employer statement and last day worked; open the claim file, send the acknowledgement letter, and start the ERISA decision clock.
steps.supporting: Claims Intake Rep, Disability Case Manager
steps.inputs: Employee claim statement, employer statement, group policy number, last day worked, contact details
steps.outputs: Registered claim file, acknowledgement letter, ERISA decision-clock start date

steps.name: Verify Coverage, Eligibility & Elimination Period
steps.description: Confirm the employee was actively at work and insured under the group STD/LTD plan, verify premium status and any pre-existing-condition limitation, and compute the elimination period (including STD-days credit toward the LTD waiting period) and maximum benefit duration.
steps.supporting: Disability Claims Intake Specialist, Benefits Administrator
steps.inputs: Group policy and plan provisions, employer eligibility and payroll records, premium status, last day worked
steps.outputs: Coverage and eligibility determination, elimination period schedule, maximum benefit duration parameters, pre-existing-condition flag

steps.name: Obtain Authorizations & Medical Evidence
steps.description: Collect signed HIPAA authorizations, request attending physician statements and treatment records, and obtain the employer job description and occupational demands needed to evaluate disability under the plan's own-occupation definition.
steps.supporting: Medical / Nurse Case Manager, Disability Case Manager
steps.inputs: Signed HIPAA authorization, attending physician statement request, treating provider list, employer job description
steps.outputs: Authorization on file, attending physician statements, treatment records, occupational demands profile

steps.name: Confirm Pre-Disability Earnings & Occupation Definition
steps.description: Validate pre-disability earnings against payroll records, establish the covered monthly earnings basis, and document the applicable definition of disability (own occupation vs any occupation and the transition point) governing adjudication.
steps.inputs: Payroll and W-2 earnings records, plan benefit formula, occupational demands profile
steps.outputs: Covered earnings basis, documented disability definition and transition point, benefit percentage confirmation

steps.name: Render Initial Liability Decision Within ERISA Timeline
steps.description: Weigh medical, occupational and eligibility evidence and issue the approve/deny decision within the ERISA disability timeline (45 days plus up to two 30-day extensions with notice), including the specific reasons, plan provisions relied on and appeal rights required by 29 CFR 2560.503-1; on approval, establish the initial disabled-life claim reserve. Non-ERISA claims follow NAIC claim settlement practice standards.
steps.supporting: Medical / Nurse Case Manager, Compliance Analyst
steps.inputs: Eligibility determination, medical evidence, occupational demands profile, covered earnings basis, ERISA decision deadline
steps.outputs: Initial liability decision, decision letter with appeal rights, benefit effective date or denial rationale, initial claim reserve

steps.name: Triage Claim by Severity & Expected Duration
steps.description: Classify the claim against evidence-based duration guidelines by diagnosis, comorbidities and job demands; assign a clinical review tier and set the medical management and follow-up cadence.
steps.inputs: Diagnosis and treatment records, duration guidelines, occupational demands profile
steps.outputs: Clinical triage tier, expected duration benchmark, medical review plan

steps.name: Conduct Clinical Review of Medical Evidence
steps.description: Review attending physician statements, diagnostics and treatment compliance for clinical consistency with the reported restrictions and limitations; identify gaps and request clarifications from treating providers.
steps.inputs: Attending physician statements, diagnostic results, treatment records, claimed restrictions and limitations
steps.outputs: Clinical review summary, evidence gap list, provider clarification requests

steps.name: Order Independent Medical Exam or Functional Capacity Evaluation
steps.description: Where evidence is conflicting or insufficient, arrange an independent medical examination, functional capacity evaluation or peer review with an appropriately credentialed examiner; refer inconsistencies suggestive of malingering or fraud to SIU.
steps.supporting: Medical / Nurse Case Manager, SIU Investigator
steps.inputs: Clinical review summary, evidence gap list, IME/FCE vendor panel
steps.outputs: IME or FCE referral, examination report, SIU referral where warranted

steps.name: Assess Functional Capacity Against Disability Definition
steps.description: Compare validated restrictions and limitations to the material duties of the claimant's own occupation (or any gainful occupation after transition), incorporating vocational and transferable-skills analysis, and conclude whether the plan's disability definition is met.
steps.supporting: Medical / Nurse Case Manager, Disability Case Manager
steps.inputs: IME/FCE report, clinical review summary, occupational demands profile, transferable skills analysis
steps.outputs: Functional capacity conclusion, disability definition determination, supported restrictions and limitations

steps.name: Document Clinical Rationale & Update Claim Plan
steps.description: Record the clinical rationale, restrictions and review conclusions in the claim file, update the expected duration and next-review date, and feed the determination to adjudication and return-to-work planning.
steps.inputs: Functional capacity conclusion, restrictions and limitations, duration benchmark
steps.outputs: Documented clinical rationale, updated claim management plan, next clinical review date

steps.name: Establish Gross Benefit From Covered Earnings
steps.description: Apply the plan benefit formula (typically 60-66.7% of covered monthly earnings, subject to plan maximums and minimums) to the validated pre-disability earnings basis to set the gross monthly benefit.
steps.inputs: Covered earnings basis, plan benefit formula, plan maximums and minimums
steps.outputs: Gross monthly benefit amount, benefit period schedule

steps.name: Identify & Apply Other-Income Offsets
steps.description: Identify deductible other income — SSDI primary and family awards, workers compensation, state disability/PFML, pension and employer salary continuation — and net them against the gross benefit per plan offset provisions, applying any minimum-benefit floor.
steps.inputs: Gross monthly benefit, SSDI award notices, workers compensation awards, state disability/PFML benefit records, pension and salary continuation data
steps.outputs: Offset schedule, net monthly benefit amount, minimum-benefit application

steps.name: Initiate SSDI Application Support & Reimbursement Agreement
steps.description: Refer eligible LTD claimants to Social Security application/advocacy support, execute the SSDI reimbursement agreement covering estimated-offset or repayment of retroactive awards, and diarize award follow-up.
steps.inputs: Claim duration outlook, SSDI eligibility indicators, advocacy vendor panel
steps.outputs: SSDI advocacy referral, signed reimbursement agreement, award follow-up diary

steps.name: Set Up Tax Withholding & Sick-Pay Reporting
steps.description: Determine the taxable portion of benefits from the employer/employee premium contribution split, apply federal and state withholding elections, and establish third-party sick pay FICA and W-2 reporting obligations.
steps.supporting: Disability Case Manager, Payment Processing Clerk
steps.inputs: Premium contribution split, withholding elections, net benefit amount, payroll reporting calendar
steps.outputs: Tax withholding setup, FICA reporting schedule, W-2/sick-pay reporting record

steps.name: Authorize & Release Recurring Benefit Payments
steps.description: Authorize the recurring payment schedule, validate payee banking details, release net benefit payments through the payment platform, and post payment records to the claim; payees flow through the enterprise sanctions screening operated under Risk & Compliance (RC-20-05) rather than a duplicated in-flow check.
steps.supporting: Disability Case Manager, Billing Operations Manager
steps.inputs: Net benefit amount, tax withholding setup, payee banking details, payment authorization
steps.outputs: Released benefit payments, payment ledger entries, explanation of benefits to claimant

l3s.name: Ongoing Disability Claim Management, Return-to-Work & Appeals

steps.name: Develop Claim Management & Contact Plan
steps.description: Set the ongoing management strategy for the claim — contact cadence with claimant, employer and providers, recertification schedule and milestone diary — proportionate to the clinical triage tier and expected duration.
steps.inputs: Clinical triage tier, expected duration benchmark, benefit period schedule
steps.outputs: Claim management plan, contact and recertification calendar, milestone diary

steps.name: Collect Periodic Proof of Continuing Disability
steps.description: Request and review continuing disability statements, updated attending physician statements and activity questionnaires at the recertification cadence; pursue non-responses and suspend benefits where proof is not furnished per plan terms.
steps.supporting: Medical / Nurse Case Manager, Disability Claims Intake Specialist
steps.inputs: Recertification calendar, continuing disability claim forms, updated attending physician statements, activity questionnaires
steps.outputs: Updated proof of continuing disability, non-response follow-ups, benefit suspension actions

steps.name: Reconcile SSDI Awards & Recover Overpayments
steps.description: On SSDI or other offset award, recalculate the net benefit retroactively, quantify any overpayment created by the retroactive award, and recover it under the reimbursement agreement via lump-sum demand or benefit reduction.
steps.inputs: SSDI award notice, signed reimbursement agreement, payment history, offset schedule
steps.outputs: Recalculated net benefit, overpayment quantification, recovery plan and collections entries

steps.name: Conduct Any-Occupation Transition Review
steps.description: Ahead of the definition change (typically at 24 months of benefits), perform a full clinical and vocational re-evaluation against the any-gainful-occupation standard, including transferable skills and labor market analysis, and determine continued eligibility.
steps.supporting: Medical Claims Reviewer, Medical / Nurse Case Manager
steps.inputs: Updated medical evidence, transferable skills analysis, labor market survey, any-occupation definition
steps.outputs: Any-occupation eligibility determination, continued-benefit or termination recommendation, transition review file

steps.name: Continue, Terminate or Settle Benefits & Communicate Decision
steps.description: Action the review outcome — continue benefits with an updated plan, negotiate a lump-sum settlement where appropriate, or terminate with a compliant letter stating reasons, plan provisions and ERISA appeal rights — and update reserves and the claim record.
steps.inputs: Transition review determination, settlement authority guidelines, reserve position
steps.outputs: Continuation, settlement or termination action, claimant decision letter with appeal rights, updated reserves

steps.name: Screen Claim for Return-to-Work Potential
steps.description: Evaluate clinical trajectory, motivation, job demands and employer environment to identify claimants with rehabilitation and return-to-work potential, and prioritize referrals to the rehab program.
steps.inputs: Clinical review summary, restrictions and limitations, occupational demands profile, claimant goals
steps.outputs: Return-to-work potential rating, rehabilitation referral list

steps.name: Develop Return-to-Work & Rehabilitation Plan
steps.description: Build an individualized plan covering treatment milestones, vocational rehabilitation services, retraining, graduated hours and target return date, agreed with the claimant, treating physician and employer.
steps.inputs: Return-to-work potential rating, treating physician input, employer job and accommodation options
steps.outputs: Agreed return-to-work plan, rehabilitation service authorizations, target return date

steps.name: Coordinate Workplace Accommodations With Employer
steps.description: Work with the employer on transitional duties, modified schedules and ADA-consistent accommodations; document employer commitments and align the accommodation with the claimant's supported restrictions.
steps.supporting: Medical / Nurse Case Manager, Account Executive
steps.inputs: Return-to-work plan, supported restrictions and limitations, employer accommodation options
steps.outputs: Accommodation agreement, transitional duty assignment, updated return-to-work plan

steps.name: Monitor Transitional Work & Apply Partial Benefit Offsets
steps.description: Track graduated return-to-work progress, apply partial/residual disability benefit calculations and work-earnings offsets per plan incentives, and adjust the plan when recovery stalls or accelerates.
steps.supporting: Medical / Nurse Case Manager, Claims Analyst
steps.inputs: Transitional work earnings, return-to-work plan milestones, partial disability provisions
steps.outputs: Partial benefit recalculations, plan progress assessments, plan adjustments

steps.name: Close Rehabilitation Case & Record Outcomes
steps.description: Confirm sustained full or accommodated return to work, close the rehabilitation case, capture outcome metrics (return rate, duration saved, cost-benefit) and feed results into program effectiveness reporting.
steps.supporting: Disability Case Manager, Claims Quality Assurance / Training Manager
steps.inputs: Sustained return-to-work confirmation, rehabilitation cost and duration data
steps.outputs: Closed rehabilitation case, outcome metrics, program effectiveness inputs

steps.name: Register Appeal & Acknowledge Within ERISA Window
steps.description: Log the claimant's appeal (claimants have at least 180 days to file under 29 CFR 2560.503-1), acknowledge receipt, provide free access to the claim file and all documents relied upon, and start the appeal decision clock.
steps.supporting: Compliance Analyst, Disability Claims Intake Specialist
steps.inputs: Appeal request, original decision letter, claim file, ERISA appeal timeline rules
steps.outputs: Registered appeal, acknowledgement letter, claim file disclosure, appeal decision deadline

steps.name: Assemble Appeal File & Assign Independent Reviewer
steps.description: Compile the complete administrative record including new evidence submitted on appeal, and assign a reviewer who was not involved in (and does not report to) the original decision-maker, with no deference to the initial denial.
steps.inputs: Administrative record, new appeal evidence, reviewer independence rules
steps.outputs: Complete appeal file, independent reviewer assignment, review plan

steps.name: Obtain Independent Clinical & Vocational Opinions
steps.description: For medical-judgment appeals, consult a health professional in the relevant specialty who did not advise on the original claim; obtain vocational opinions where occupation capacity is disputed, and share any new rationale with the claimant before deciding.
steps.supporting: Medical / Nurse Case Manager, Claims Examiner
steps.inputs: Complete appeal file, specialty reviewer panel, disputed clinical and vocational issues
steps.outputs: Independent clinical opinion, vocational opinion, claimant disclosure of new rationale

steps.name: Render Appeal Determination Within Regulatory Timeline
steps.description: Decide the appeal within 45 days (one 45-day extension with notice for special circumstances), and issue a determination letter stating the specific reasons, plan provisions, scientific/clinical judgment basis and the claimant's right to civil action under ERISA 502(a).
steps.inputs: Complete appeal file, independent opinions, appeal decision deadline
steps.outputs: Appeal determination, compliant determination letter, reinstated benefits or upheld denial

steps.name: Refer Exhausted Appeals to Litigation Counsel
steps.description: When administrative remedies are exhausted and suit is filed or threatened, hand the certified administrative record to litigation counsel, support discovery and deposition needs, and track outcomes and remediation lessons back into claim practices.
steps.inputs: Upheld denial, certified administrative record, litigation notice
steps.outputs: Litigation referral package, certified record, lessons-learned feedback

l4s.name: FMLA & State Leave Intake and Eligibility Determination

steps.name: Receive Leave Request & Open Absence Case
steps.description: Capture the employee's leave request (or employer notification of a potentially qualifying absence) on behalf of the group client, record the reason, requested dates and leave type, and open the absence case.
steps.inputs: Employee leave request, employer notification, absence reason and requested dates, employer plan rules
steps.outputs: Opened absence case, recorded leave reason and dates, intake confirmation

steps.name: Determine Eligibility & Issue Notice Within Five Business Days
steps.description: Verify FMLA eligibility (12 months service, 1,250 hours, 50-employee/75-mile worksite) and applicable state leave eligibility, and issue the eligibility plus rights-and-responsibilities notice (WH-381 equivalent) within five business days per 29 CFR 825.300.
steps.supporting: Compliance Analyst, Disability Claims Intake Specialist
steps.inputs: Employer service and hours records, worksite headcount data, federal and state leave eligibility rules
steps.outputs: Eligibility determination, eligibility and rights-and-responsibilities notice, state-leave eligibility mapping

steps.name: Obtain & Review Medical Certification
steps.description: Request medical certification with a 15-calendar-day return window, review for completeness and sufficiency, allow a cure period for deficiencies, and arrange authentication, clarification or second/third opinions where authorized.
steps.inputs: Medical certification forms, healthcare provider responses, certification sufficiency criteria
steps.outputs: Complete and sufficient certification, cure-period notices, second/third opinion results

steps.name: Designate Leave & Issue Designation Notice
steps.description: Determine whether the absence qualifies, designate it as FMLA and/or state leave, count it against the entitlement, and issue the written designation notice within five business days of having sufficient information, including the amount of leave counted where known.
steps.inputs: Complete certification, eligibility determination, leave entitlement balances
steps.outputs: Leave designation decision, designation notice, entitlement deduction schedule

steps.name: Map Concurrent Entitlements Across FMLA, State Leave, STD & ADA
steps.description: Identify all entitlements the absence triggers — federal FMLA, state family/medical and paid family leave programs, the STD claim and potential ADA accommodation — set them to run concurrently where permitted, and link the absence case to any companion disability claim.
steps.inputs: Designation decision, state PFML program rules, companion STD claim record, ADA accommodation indicators
steps.outputs: Concurrency map, linked disability claim reference, ADA referral flag

steps.name: Track Continuous & Intermittent Leave Usage
steps.description: Record leave usage against the 12-week (or state-specific) entitlement in the smallest increment the employer uses, manage intermittent and reduced-schedule tracking, and respond to employee entitlement-balance requests within the 30-day window.
steps.inputs: Reported absences, entitlement balances, employer increment rules, intermittent leave schedule
steps.outputs: Updated leave balances, intermittent usage log, entitlement-balance responses

steps.name: Monitor Recertification & Fitness-for-Duty Requirements
steps.description: Diarize and request recertifications at permitted intervals (generally every 30 days or per minimum duration, every 6 months for chronic conditions), and administer fitness-for-duty certification requirements before return where the employer policy requires them.
steps.inputs: Certification durations, recertification rules, employer fitness-for-duty policy
steps.outputs: Recertification requests and results, fitness-for-duty certifications, non-compliance escalations

steps.name: Coordinate Leave With Disability Benefits & Payroll
steps.description: Synchronize absence status with the companion STD/state PFML benefit so pay sources do not duplicate, feed leave status to employer payroll for pay and benefits-continuation handling, and reconcile discrepancies between leave and claim records.
steps.supporting: Disability Case Manager, Payment Processing Clerk
steps.inputs: Leave balances, STD/PFML payment records, employer payroll calendar
steps.outputs: Synchronized pay and leave status, payroll feed, discrepancy resolutions

steps.name: Report Absence Status & Trends to Employer
steps.description: Deliver recurring absence reporting to the employer client — open cases, designations, balances, intermittent usage patterns and absence trends — supporting workforce planning and compliance audit needs.
steps.inputs: Absence case data, leave balances, trend analytics, employer reporting requirements
steps.outputs: Employer absence status reports, trend analysis, compliance audit extracts

steps.name: Close Leave Case & Confirm Job Restoration
steps.description: On return or exhaustion, close the absence case, confirm the employer restored the employee to the same or an equivalent position (or document key-employee/exhaustion exceptions), and retain records per FMLA's three-year retention requirement.
steps.inputs: Return-to-work date, restoration confirmation, exhaustion or exception documentation
steps.outputs: Closed absence case, job restoration confirmation, retained compliance records

notes: Shared-stream references (checked against vs-outline.json, not duplicated): payee sanctions/AML screening lives in Risk & Compliance RC-20-05 — recurring disability benefit payees are screened by that enterprise program, so no in-flow OFAC step was added (unlike life lump-sum disbursements where the relocations carry one); escheatment of uncashed benefit checks routes to Finance F-11-05; formal complaints route to Customer Service OC-14-03; fraud referrals leverage SIU roles but investigations execute under Claims Intake-to-Settlement.

Relocated steps: none of the 8 entries in life-relocations.json target this stream — all belong to life claims FNOL (CI-02-01-S07), life/annuity in-force servicing (CI-04-05-S01..S05) and life/annuity new-business underwriting (CI-06-05-S01/S02). Zero relocations were absorbed here.

Design decisions: 3 L3s mirror the industry-standard group disability lifecycle — adjudication (intake/eligibility/elimination period, clinical and functional review, benefit calc with SSDI/WC/PFML offsets), ongoing management (recertification, 24-month own-occ→any-occ transition review, RTW/vocational rehab, ERISA appeals with the 180-day filing / 45+45-day decision / independent-reviewer rules of 29 CFR 2560.503-1), and absence administration as an outsourced employer service (FMLA 5-business-day eligibility and designation notices per 29 CFR 825.300, 15-day medical certification, intermittent tracking, state PFML/STD/ADA concurrency, job restoration).

Roles: leads are day-to-day doers from role-inventory.json verbatim, anchored on the Life & Retirement set (Disability Claims Intake Specialist, Disability Case Manager) plus Medical / Nurse Case Manager, Medical Claims Reviewer, Benefits Administrator, Claims Examiner (appeals lead chosen deliberately as a different decision-maker than the Disability Case Manager, satisfying ERISA reviewer-independence), Tax Analyst and Payment Processing Clerk for tax/disbursement steps.

Deliverable systems of record from app-inventory.json: Claims Management Platform (claim decision package, FCE determination, offset worksheet, continuing review determination, RTW plan), Document & Forms Management (ERISA appeal letter, FMLA designation notice), BI / Reporting (employer absence reporting). One deliverable per L4, placed on its pivotal step.

All L3/L4 names are disability/absence-specific and do not reuse any P&C L3 names from vs-outline.json (no existing stream contains disability, FMLA, leave or return-to-work content — verified by keyword scan).

Sources: [DOL Fact Sheet 28D — FMLA employer notification](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fact-sheets/28d-fmla-employer%20notification), [29 CFR 825.300 — employer notice requirements](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/subtitle-B/chapter-V/subchapter-C/part-825/subpart-C/section-825.300), [DOL FMLA leave process](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fmla/FMLA-leave-process), [DeBofsky — LTD elimination periods](https://www.debofsky.com/articles/elimination-period-long-term-disability-policy/), [Tucker Disability — LTD/SSDI offset mechanics](https://tuckerdisability.com/blog/ltd/ltd-and-ssdi-at-the-same-time/), [DisabilitySecrets — ERISA disability benefits and appeal timelines](https://www.disabilitysecrets.com/resources/disability/employee/worker-disability/erisa-benefits.htm), [Bryant Legal Group — own-occ to any-occ transition](https://bryantlg.com/blog/how-long-can-you-stay-on-long-term-disability-it-depends/)

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (2026-06-11) — verification results: (a) Industry/regulatory accuracy web-checked against primary sources: ERISA disability initial decision = 45 days + up to two 30-day extensions (105 days max), appeal filing window ≥180 days, appeal decision 45 days + one 45-day extension with independent non-deferential reviewer and specialty consultation, all confirmed via [eCFR 29 CFR 2560.503-1](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/subtitle-B/chapter-XXV/subchapter-G/part-2560/section-2560.503-1) and [DOL EBSA claims-procedure compliance guide](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/ebsa/about-ebsa/our-activities/resource-center/publications/group-health-and-disability-plans-benefit-claims-procedure-regulation); FMLA 5-business-day eligibility and designation notices and 15-calendar-day certification window confirmed via [eCFR 29 CFR 825.300](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/subtitle-B/chapter-V/subchapter-C/part-825/subpart-C/section-825.300) and [eCFR 29 CFR 825.305](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/subtitle-B/chapter-V/subchapter-C/part-825/subpart-C/section-825.305). Step ordering (eligibility → evidence → earnings basis → decision; suitability/offsets before payment release; appeals after exhaustion of initial decision) matches group-disability practice. (b) Wiring audit: all 19 distinct lead/supporting role names matched role-inventory.json verbatim with zero near-misses; all 3 sorApplications (Claims Management Platform, Document & Forms Management, BI / Reporting) confirmed in app-inventory.json. (c) Duplication audit: keyword scan (disability|FMLA|absence|leave|return-to-work|vocational|SSDI|elimination period|STD|LTD|paid family) across all 29 streams in vs-outline.json returned zero hits; the three shared-stream codes cited were verified to exist exactly as referenced (RC-20-05 = Financial crime, sanctions & AML compliance; F-11-05 = Escheatment and unclaimed property reporting; OC-14-03 = Formal complaint handling and regulatory response). (d) Relocations re-verified: all 8 life-relocations.json codes (CI-02-01-S07, CI-04-05-S01..S05, CI-06-05-S01/S02) target other streams; none mandated here.

CHANGES MADE during adversarial review: (1) Life-only rule fix — renamed L3 'Ongoing Claim Management, Return-to-Work & Appeals' to 'Ongoing Disability Claim Management, Return-to-Work & Appeals' because the bare 'Ongoing Claim Management' lead-in read as a generic claims-area name usable by any P&C line. (2) Industry-accuracy fix — added initial disabled-life claim reserve establishment to 'Render Initial Liability Decision Within ERISA Timeline' (description + 'initial claim reserve' output): group disability carriers book the claim reserve at approval, but the original design only referenced reserves at the continuation/termination step, leaving the reserve lifecycle without an origin. No steps were added, deleted, or reordered — the flow, role wiring, deliverables and shared-stream handoffs all survived verification intact.
